notes: Mayor Watters welcomed everyone and called the meeting to order.

notes: Councillor MacDonald read the land acknowledgement.

items.title: Addendums and Corrections to the Agenda
notes: None.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest Under the Municipal Conflict of Interest
notes: Act
Councillor Jefferson declared a conflict of pecuniary interest with respect to agenda item 8.1, the Fergus BIA Budget as she owns property within the business improvement catchment area.

items.title: Dan Wilson, CAO outlined the agenda for the day highlighting the
notes: linkages between the Strategic Plan, the Business Plan and the Draft Budget. He noted the property taxation impact by area and the overall Township Property Taxation impact resulting in a 3.86% increase in taxation. He outlined the budget reductions already made by the senior management team in the amount of $676,675 and the enhancements to current services contemplated as follows:
a. Radio Station Communications (signed agreement)
b. Health & Safety Compliance and Operating Procedures (staffing) c. Purchasing & Risk (staffing)
d. IT security and risk mitigation
e. Paid parking administration and year-round parking enforcement f. Funding for snow plowing, sidewalk plowing, PW fleet maintenance, and safety devices
g. Project management and construction inspection (staffing) h. Downtowns budget
i. 4 new crossing guards (staffing)
j. Wastewater environmental protection (staffing)
k. Recreation facility operations and maintenance (staffing) l. Trail maintenance level of service (staffing)
m. Economic Development capacity (staffing) – MSC Related n. Housing and planning policy capacity (staffing)
o. Parks development planning and parks infrastructure project management (staffing)
p. Asset management investment
D. Wilson outlined the funding summary and responded to a question from Councillor Wilton regarding the application of the insurance savings to asset management rather than the tax rate.

items.title: Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
notes: provided an overview and summary of the draft budget, including asset management, general budget information and the public engagement process undertaken. He also reiterated the asset management planning recommendations and the proposed 2.5% increase to the fees and charges.

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the tax supported operating budget, including operating budget facts, how the budget works and the process undertaken, funding challenges, impact areas and assessment growth.
M. Bradey provided an overview of the draft capital budget, including the sources of financing and the gross expenditures by service area.
Adam McNabb review the Debt Analysis, debt payments by service type and the projected debt as a percentage of revenue.

Staff responded to questions regarding future use of the municipal accommodation tax and parking revenues, advocacy for sustainable government funding sources, and staff compliment comparisons with other municipalities.
Mayor Watters called for a 7 minute break.

items.title: Proposed 2026 Levels of Service in BIA Catchments
notes: Report from A. Gilmore, Managing Director of Community Services Adam Gilmore, Managing Director of Community Services provided an overview of the report, indicating the report outlines the proposed Levels of Service, including maintenance, waste collection, washroom cleaning, event support and other services. He indicated Council’s endorsement of the recommended 2026 levels of service will guide operational planning and budgeting beginning in January 2026.

Staff responded to questions regarding support of events such as Monster Month, inclusion of more garbage receptacles and increased pick up, sidewalk cleaning, more benches and bike racks in Fergus, improved wayfinding, and future plans for the Weigh Scale building.

items.title: Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad Update
notes: Report from K. Beirnes, Manager of Buildings & Property K. Beirnes, Manager of Buildings & Property provided an overview of the project, indicating staff and the Bissell Park Working Group have developed two options now under consideration. These options are as follows:

Option 1: Replace Like-for-Like – This option includes replacing the pad, boards, lighting, basketball nets, and constructing an accessible pathway. It provides a modernized facility that maintains its current functionality and supports year-round recreational use.

Option 2: Replace Like-for-Like with Refrigeration Infrastructure (preferred option, provided it can be constructed within the current approved budget) – This option mirrors the above but includes installing refrigeration lines and a recirculation pump. Although it does not include the refrigeration plant itself, it prepares the site for future installation, reducing long-term disruption and positioning the facility for improved winter usability when/if additional funding becomes available.
K. Beirnes outlined the next steps and the proposed timeline.

Discussion ensued and staff responded to questions regarding future design options, refinement of the cost estimates with detailed design, allowing for future refrigeration and anticipated changes to operating procedures and volunteers.

items.title: Business Park Pricing Policy - 2026
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development provided an overview of the report and responded to questions regarding use of realty services and the sales interest.

items.title: D. Wilson, CAO provided an overview of the proposed Staffing Strategy
notes: for 2026, indicating new staff positions are required for the following reasons:
 Growth Demands: As the Township continues to grow,
departments require more staffing to meet the needs of our community and maintain levels of service. In some cases, departments are restructured in order to accommodate planned growth.
 Legislation: Ensure various provincial and federal legislation are met.

 New Services: Provide new services and/or programs as a He reviewed the position request procedure, the decision aid matrix, and the funding formula used. He outlined the proposed 2026 new staffing as follows:
Economic Development Officer
Human Resources Health and Safety / Human Resources Assistant Purchasing and Risk Analyst
Junior Construction Inspector
Labourer - Infrastructure Services
Environmental Protection Officer
Capital Project Manager
Facility Attendant
Labourer - Community Services
Parks Maintenance Crew Members
Policy and Housing Planner Permanent
Discussion ensued and staff responded to questions.
Mayor Watters called for a lunch break, with the meeting resuming at 1pm with the scheduled delegations.
Delegations @ 1:00 pm
Councillor Jefferson, having declared a conflict of interest with respect to the Fergus BIA Budget left the Chamber and therefore did not participate in discussions.

Fred Gordon, BIA Administrator provided an overview and highlights of the various activities of the Fergus BIA over the past year. He presented the budget adopted at the November 5th annual general meeting.

Maclean Hann, Chair Elora BIA provided an overview of the various successful events held over the past year. He noted the budget was approved with a levy increase at the annual general meeting held on November 10, 2025.
Mayor Watters redirected Members back to complete discussions regarding the staffing strategy.
Staff outlined the remaining proposed positions, positions beyond 2028 and responded to questions.

items.title: 2026 Fees and Charges By-law
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report, noting pre-budget direction from Council to increase fees and charges by 2.4%, unless other factors require an increase that is more or less than the prescribed amount. He responded to questions regarding the community hall rate, fire services fees, planning services fees and fees related to special events.

items.title: 2026 Draft Business Plan
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report and responded to questions regarding the transition from the Economic Prosperity & Growth Advisory Committee to the Municipal Service Corporation, the multi-use recreational facility project and projects for Strathallen, Confederation and Webster parks

items.title: Tax Supported Operating Budget
notes: Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance and Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the 2026 tax supported operating budget summary. He reviewed the average residential tax bill breakdown and noted the significant areas impacting the tax support operating budget.

Staff from the various departments responded to questions regarding the fire rescue salary market review, implementation of AI, invasive species spraying, traffic calming measures and continued monitoring, and the street light reserve.

items.title: 2026 Capital Budget
notes: Mark Bradey outlined the minor changes to the Capital Budget and responded to questions regarding the need for a disaster recovery site, the various wayfinding signage initiatives, the Elora Cemetery fencing, and details regarding the maintenance at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre and the Weigh scale building.
Mayor Watters called for a 5 minute recess.

items.title: Parking Lot

a. Staffing Strategy – Policy Planner Housing position
